clue.text: Ordered aabcehilpt

parts.note: the string of ten letters is the answer's own letters set out from A to Z, so it is a word put in order of the letters

explanation.walkthrough: The jumble looks like nonsense, but it is the answer's letters sorted from A to Z, which is exactly what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged in the order of the letters from A to Z is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Give permission to divide up eastern food

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for divide is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to divide is to cut

explanation.definitionFit: A salad leaf is an item of food, eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Damp patch finally with mud I spread

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word patch
mud spread about is scattered, so the letters of mud and I are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Humid air is moist or damp, heavy with water vapour.

clue.text: Famous German city

definitions.meaning: Otto von ..., the nineteenth-century Prussian statesman who unified Germany
the state capital of North Dakota in the USA

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Iron Chancellor of Germany and to the capital city of North Dakota.

clue.text: Dizzy, take pole, right, and head off wobbling on top of roof? One might

indicators.note: dizzy means spinning and confused, so the following letters are whirled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of the word wobbling is its opening letter
the top of the word roof is its first letter

explanation.surface: A giddy acrobat with a balancing pole teeters high above a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is TAKEPOLE, RIGHT, W (head of wobbling) and R (top of roof); 'Dizzy' rearranges them. 'One might' refers back to the whole scene of wobbling up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-wire artiste might well wobble atop a roof while carrying a balancing pole, as the clue pictures.

clue.text: Talented head of airforce exiting chopper

indicators.note: the head of the word airforce is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gifted air force commander climbs out of a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter, fitting the air force, but here it is a meat cleaver.
explanation.definitionFit: A talented person is bright and able, a synonym of smart or gifted.

clue.text: Assume one's quit job

parts.note: to posit is to assume or suppose

explanation.definitionFit: A post is a position of employment, a synonym of job.

clue.text: Hash — it usually smells nice

definitions.meaning: a hash is a jumbled mixture or medley
a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for its scent

clue.text: Charge for keeping silver in shop

Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

clue.text: Move fast when losing a race

clue.text: Head back with doctor to area where you might see caribou

definitions.text: area where you might see caribou

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

clue.text: One won't drink to Attlee reforms

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A total abstainer is someone who never drinks alcohol, so the adjective describes one who won't drink.

clue.text: Finish third bit of trout one's smoked

clue.text: Most dowdy female fashion — I'm upset with Queen

clue.text: One quivers in the wind

parts.note: a tall marsh grass trembles in the breeze, and a vibrating strip sounds in a woodwind instrument

parts.words: One who reads out for others to scribe? Moi?
parts.note: someone who speaks aloud for a secretary to take down, and also an autocrat demanding it be all about me

clue.text: Lover's knot, we hear

parts.note: a bow is a knot tied with loops

clue.text: Learned English — impolite about it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: Be sitting on judge's carpet

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: This may help build evidence up on base criminal
